faqs.answer: Because honey has almost no air in it. A cup of flour is mostly air between the particles, so it weighs 120 grams. A cup of honey is dense liquid sugar, so it weighs 336 grams. Nearly three times as much.

howToSteps.name: Use a liquid measuring cup
howToSteps.text: Honey is a liquid, so measure it in a glass liquid measuring cup with a spout, not a dry measuring cup. Set the cup on the counter and read the level at eye level.

howToSteps.name: Oil the cup first
howToSteps.text: Wipe the inside of the cup with a little neutral oil, or rinse it with hot water. The honey will slide out cleanly instead of clinging to the sides.

howToSteps.name: Pour to the line
howToSteps.text: Pour the honey slowly and let it settle. Honey pours thick, so wait a few seconds before checking the level. It keeps moving after you stop pouring.

howToSteps.name: Or weigh it
howToSteps.text: Put the bowl on the scale, tare it to zero, and pour the honey in. One cup is 336 grams, one tablespoon is 21 grams. No sticky cup to wash.

title: Honey: Cups to Grams Converter
tutorial: Honey is heavy. A cup of it weighs 336 grams, nearly three times what a cup of flour weighs. That is because honey is mostly sugar and water with almost no air in it. It pours slowly and it weighs every bit of what it looks like.

The number comes from King Arthur Baking's chart: 21 grams per tablespoon. Sixteen tablespoons make a cup, so 16 × 21 = 336 grams. Measure honey in a liquid measuring cup, the glass kind with a spout, not a dry measuring cup. Honey is a liquid, and a liquid cup is the only way to read the level properly.

The sticky part is the measuring. Honey clings to the cup and half of it stays behind when you pour. The fix is simple: lightly oil the cup first, or rinse it with hot water. The honey slides right out. Weighing it on the scale is even easier. Put the bowl on the scale, tare it, and pour until the number is right.

Use the converter in either direction. A recipe in cups becomes grams for the scale, and grams become cups when you are working without one. The anchors are easy: half a cup is 168 grams, a quarter cup is 84 grams, and one tablespoon is 21 grams.

One thing worth knowing: crystallized honey weighs the same as liquid honey. Crystals are just the sugars settling out. The honey has not lost anything. Warm the jar gently in hot water and it goes liquid again, same weight, same sweetness.
